findings.diagnosis: The scorer underestimates contradiction risk when a cut leaves a short clause fragment (a subject/NP or function-word-only span) that lacks its predicate, auxiliary, negation scope, or required complement; such pre-cut fragments, read alone, often assert something the rest of the sentence later reverses.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1570','en_us_87','en_us_105','en_us_140','en_us_741']: these cases all show the policy keeping cuts that isolate brief subject/fragment spans or split scope-bearing items (negation/auxiliaries), producing high contra or contra_kill. (5)

edit.text: If the span before a cut is a short subject/NP or a clause fragment lacking its predicate, auxiliary, negation scope, or required complement, treat that cut as high contradiction risk and rank it low.

findings.diagnosis: The scorer undervalues cohesion loss from splitting heads from their required complements (prepositions and their objects, 'of' phrases, verb complements, or a main noun and its postnominal modifiers); cuts that sever these relationships often degrade joined translation quality.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_455','en_us_360','en_us_140','en_us_105','en_us_1352']: these examples show the policy cutting between prepositions/heads and their complements or inside long noun/modifier sequences, harming cohesion in the joined text. (5)

edit.text: Avoid cuts that separate heads from their required complements (prepositions + objects, 'of' phrases, verb complements, or a noun and its postnominal modifiers); such splits markedly reduce cohesion and should be scored lower.
